run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T16:58:47Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is firing because frontend-proxy's server span operation "ingress" intermittently returns HTTP 503, and those 503s are recorded as STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans, giving a small but non-zero per-second error-span rate. The 503s are not application errors from the demo backends: frontend-proxy's own Envoy access logs show every failure with response detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} on the "frontend" upstream (ClusterIP 100.70.94.93:8080), i.e. the connection to the frontend workload was terminated before a response started, and Envoy answered 503 itself (95 bytes sent). The pattern is continuous and low-grade: 31.48 error ingress spans against 22,490 non-error ingress spans over 15:58:47–17:06:09 (~0.14%), present in every 10-minute bucket with data (4.52, 10.53, 5.26, 8.39) and in the access log from the earliest readable minute (16:32:01) through 17:02:29, so the alert trips on a couple of resets falling into its evaluation window rather than on a surge. The alert's reported value 0.033333 equals the 2-minute per-second rate of ERROR ingress spans at 16:59:47 (0.0222 at 16:58:47, 0.0333 one minute later), consistent with an error-establishment alert on a near-zero threshold. The frontend itself shows no failure signs: zero ERROR counts on all of its own spans (server GET, Next.js route spans and every downstream gRPC client span to ad, cart, checkout, product-catalog and recommendation), pod Running/Ready with 0 restarts, deployment 1/1. What the environment does show on the frontend is resource squeeze: its container runs ~0.04–0.053 cores against a 100m CPU limit with 25–38% of CFS periods throttled for the whole window, which is a plausible mechanism for a Node.js server destroying keep-alive sockets just as Envoy reuses them, but the exact keep-alive/idle-timeout lever (frontend server side vs frontend-proxy Envoy cluster pool) could not be read, so that mechanism remains a hypothesis rather than an observation.

claims.text: frontend-proxy has exactly two span operations: "ingress" (SPAN_KIND_SERVER) and "router frontend egress" (SPAN_KIND_CLIENT); over the authorised window the ingress operation accrued 31.484375 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans versus 22490 STATUS_CODE_UNSET, while "router frontend egress" accrued 0 STATUS_CODE_ERROR versus 22520.46875 STATUS_CODE_UNSET — so the only failing spans of this service are its inbound server spans.

frontend-proxy's access logs show the failing requests are HTTP 503 with response flag UC and response detail upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} against upstream cluster "frontend" (upstream host 100.70.94.93:8080, which is the frontend Service ClusterIP:8080), from user-agent python-requests, with 95 bytes sent — Envoy's own 503 body. Observed examples run 16:50:15.550 through 17:02:29.955 on paths /api/products/*, /api/cart, /api/recommendations, /api/data/ and /.

The same 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} failures are present in the earliest readable part of the window (21 lines between 16:32:01.988 and 16:46:25.124) interleaved with successful 200/308 via_upstream lines (all 100 access-log lines between 16:50:01.123 and 16:50:10.868 were 200 or 308), so the condition is continuous and low-rate, not a spike near the alert start.

In 10-minute buckets that have data (span-metric samples begin only at 16:31:47), ingress STATUS_CODE_ERROR increases are 4.524653333333333 (from 16:36:09), 10.526315789473683 (16:46:09), 5.263157894736842 (16:56:09) and 8.386176507936508 (17:06:09) against 3999.79, 6267.37, 6347.37 and 4822.05 non-error ingress spans, i.e. a steady low error fraction with no upward ramp before the alert started at 16:58:47.

The alert annotation's value 0.033333333333333326 is reproduced by the 2-minute per-second rate of frontend-proxy ingress ERROR spans: 0.02222222222222222 at 16:58:47 and 0.033333333333333326 at 16:59:47 (also 0.0333 at 16:41:47 and 16:45:47), i.e. the alert value corresponds to a handful of error spans inside a short window, not to a large error ratio.

The frontend service shows no error of its own: every ERROR series for service_name="frontend" is 0 across its server spans ("GET", "GET /", "GET /api/cart", "GET /api/data", "GET /api/products/{productId}", "GET /api/recommendations", "POST /api/cart", "POST /api/checkout"), its internal Next.js route spans, and its gRPC client spans (AdService/GetAds, CartService/GetCart, CartService/AddItem, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, ProductCatalogService/GetProduct, RecommendationService/ListRecommendations).

Across all services, the only ERROR-status span counts above zero in the window are frontend-proxy "ingress" (31.484375), ad "flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream" (2.0377358490566038), fraud-detection "flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream" (2.0408163265306123) and recommendation "/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream" (4.0625) — no downstream demo service reports request failures.

The frontend and frontend-proxy pods are Running with restartCount 0 and all 21 otel-demo deployments report 1 desired/1 ready/1 available/1 updated replica; the frontend container has limits cpu 100m / memory 200Mi and frontend-proxy limits cpu 30m / memory 50Mi.

The frontend container is CPU-throttled throughout the window: throttle ratio (throttled CFS periods / CFS periods) stays between 0.2535 and 0.3794 for container "frontend" in pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh, while frontend-proxy's container stays between 0.0471 and 0.0791; frontend CPU usage is 0.0399–0.0533 cores against its 100m limit and frontend-proxy 0.0111–0.0141 cores against 30m.

Memory is not near its limit: max working-set over the window is 128720896 B (~123 MiB) for the frontend container (limit 200Mi) and 20627456 B (~20 MiB) for frontend-proxy (limit 50Mi); no memory-failure evidence was observed for either pod.
All five cluster nodes are Ready with MemoryPressure, DiskPressure, PIDPressure and NetworkUnavailable all False, so node-level pressure does not explain the resets.

All otel-demo ReplicaSets were created at 16:18:50–16:18:52 (frontend-675fd7b5c5 and frontend-proxy-6b4d584985 included) except flagd-7f6c6df658, created 16:20:44 with the older flagd-c47676d99 left at 0 desired — a namespace-wide (re)start plus a later flagd rollover, both before the alert start and before the span-metric data begins.

The only ConfigMaps present in otel-demo are flagd-config, kube-root-ca.crt, otel-collector and product-catalog-products; no frontend-proxy/Envoy configuration object is readable there, so the upstream cluster's keep-alive/idle-timeout settings could not be inspected.

The fraud-detection pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-wvrwx carries restartCount 1 with lastState.terminated.reason OOMKilled and exitCode 137; it is a separate observation in the same namespace with no error spans and no trace evidence tying it to frontend-proxy's ingress 503s.

Primary explanation: the alert is firing because Envoy on frontend-proxy fails a small subset of requests with 503 when a pooled upstream connection to the frontend service is terminated before a response starts (UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}); each such 503 becomes a STATUS_CODE_ERROR "ingress" span, and a few resets inside the alert's short evaluation window push the error rate above its (near-zero) threshold — matching the observed 0.0222/s at 16:58:47 and 0.0333/s at 16:59:47.

Deeper candidate: the terminating peer is the frontend workload's HTTP server closing idle keep-alive sockets that the proxy reuses. frontend runs at ~0.04–0.053 cores against a 100m limit with 25–38% of CFS periods throttled for the whole window, which would make socket-idle timers fire late/unpredictably relative to arriving requests and produce exactly this reset-before-response pattern; the frontend SDK also records no error for those requests because no request is completed there. This mechanism is plausible but not demonstrated — the frontend server's keep-alive settings and stderr/stdout logs were not readable.

Alternative candidate for the same symptom: the fault may sit in the frontend-proxy Envoy upstream connection pool (e.g. an upstream HTTP keep-alive/idle_timeout or max_requests_per_connection setting that retires a connection while a request is being written). Evidence cannot separate this from a frontend-side socket close, because the Envoy configuration is baked into the image and no frontend-proxy ConfigMap exists in otel-demo.

Unresolved: the namespace-wide restart at 16:18:50–16:18:52 (all ReplicaSets recreated, flagd rolled again at 16:20:44) could have introduced the configuration state that now produces the resets, but span-metric samples begin only at 16:31:47, so there is no pre-16:31:47 error baseline to show whether the 503 UC rate rose because of it; coincidence in time is not evidence of causation.

Rejected: a failing demo backend (product-catalog, cart, recommendation, checkout, etc.) causing frontend 5xx. frontend's gRPC client spans to all of those services have zero ERROR counts, the frontend's own server/route spans have zero errors, and the failing requests carry Envoy's upstream-reset 503 with 95 bytes sent rather than an application error response — the requests never produced a frontend handler span.

Rejected: node-level resource pressure or node unavailability causing connection resets. All five nodes are Ready with no MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure/NetworkUnavailable, both involved pods are Running/Ready with restartCount 0, and no other service in the namespace shows comparable request errors.

The surface state of both entities involved is healthy and stable: frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-p6mgt and frontend-675fd7b5c5-8qrfh are Running/Ready with restartCount 0, every otel-demo deployment reports 1/1 ready, and no pod in the namespace is Pending/Failed or in BackOff — so the alert is not explained by a crashed or unavailable workload.

The impact inside frontend-proxy is small in share terms: 31.484375 error ingress spans against 22490 non-error ingress spans over the same 67 minutes is about 0.14%, and the failures are spread evenly across the four 10-minute buckets with data rather than concentrated after the alert start, which argues against a new large-scale outage and for a persistent low-grade connection-reset condition crossing a very sensitive threshold.

gaps: No Prometheus rule named RequestErrorRate is loaded in the queried Prometheus (list_prometheus_rules returned no_data), so the alert's exact expression, threshold and for-duration are unknown; the match between the annotation value 0.0333 and the 2-minute error-span rate is a numerical correlation, not proof of the rule body.

Span metrics for frontend-proxy/frontend begin only at 16:31:47 inside the authorised window, and kube-state-metrics series (kube_deployment_status_replicas_*, kube_pod_owner, kube_replicaset_owner) returned nothing for namespace otel-demo, so there is no pre-16:31:47 baseline: whether the 503 UC rate rose, or was already present before the window, cannot be determined.

The frontend-proxy Envoy configuration is not exposed in any readable object (the only otel-demo ConfigMaps are flagd-config, kube-root-ca.crt, otel-collector and product-catalog-products), so the upstream cluster's keep-alive/idle_timeout/max_requests_per_connection settings could not be verified.

The frontend container produced no stdout/stderr lines for 16:30:00–17:06:09 (fetch_pod_logs read 0 bytes for the current and no previous instance), so the server-side view of socket closes/keep-alive timeouts could not be checked.

Kubernetes events for otel-demo returned no rows in the authorised window, so the timing of the fraud-detection OOMKill (restartCount 1, exitCode 137) and of any other transient pod event could not be dated.

frontend-proxy access logs could not be read end-to-end: the 4 MiB read limit cut the stream at 16:52:17 in one query and 17:02:40 in another, so log content after ~17:02:40 and parts of 16:19–16:32 remain unread, and the first 503 observed (16:32:01.988) is only the earliest readable one, not necessarily the first occurrence.
Change history is not integrated, so no configuration/manifest change preceding the resets could be correlated.
Frontend latency behaviour was not established against a comparable baseline, so slow-request contributions to the resets are unknown.

Whether the load-generator propagated these 503s to end users is not observable in the evidence; the load-generator logs contained no error/503 lines in the matching portions, but that is not proof of absence.
next_steps: Read the frontend-proxy Envoy bootstrap/cluster config (baked into ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend-proxy) and compare its upstream HTTP keep-alive/idle_timeout and max_requests_per_connection for the "frontend" cluster with the frontend server's keep-alive timeout, to decide which side must change.
Capture frontend application logs (enable stdout logging or a sidecar) so socket closes/resets around the 503 timestamps can be seen directly.

Evaluate whether the frontend container limit (cpu 100m, memory 200Mi) is adequate given ~0.05 cores sustained and 25–38% CFS throttling; a CPU-limit increase is a candidate mitigation to test, not a proven fix.

Inspect the frontend-proxy access logs for the full window with a streamed/aggregated query to get an exact 503 UC timeline and to confirm the ~35–45 second recurrence cadence observed in the sampled log excerpts.
Check kube-state-metrics namespace coverage for otel-demo so deployment/replicaset/pod ownership and availability can be trended rather than only read live.
Consider alerting on the error ratio or a minimum absolute error rate rather than an error rate above zero, since this alert trips on roughly 3–4 resets in a 2-minute window (0.14% of requests).
